target_customer: Refugees and displaced people, and the healthcare, legal and social service providers that need interpretation; paid services subsidize free access
problem: People in crises cannot reach a translator when they need one. Tarjimly connects them to volunteer bilingual translators through chat and an app, and sells paid interpretation to institutions.
business_model: Nonprofit: grants and donations plus pay per minute interpretation and per word translation

founders.name: Atif Javed
prior_employers: Monarch (product lead for data and AI teams, later role)
education: MIT graduate per 2017 coverage; degree not stated
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no education. News coverage calls both founders MIT graduates.

founders.name: Aziz Alghunaim
education: MIT, bachelor's and master's in Computer Science, 2015

technical_complexity.rationale: A Messenger bot and later app matching users to volunteers is standard engineering; the hard part was recruiting and vetting thousands of volunteers.

defensibility.rationale: A large volunteer network across many languages (reported as 56,000 plus) is hard to replicate quickly, but the matching technology is not.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rather than a competitor copying it, a fellow nonprofit, CLEAR Global, absorbed it in 2026 and moved its volunteers into Translators without Borders.

market_need_then: After the January 2017 US travel ban the founders launched a Messenger bot; by February 2018 TechCrunch reported 2,500 plus translators had helped over 1,000 refugees, and an independent app was coming.

branding.domain_note: Uses tarjimly.org. No purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven, humanitarian; says all profits fund free language access

branding.community_and_virality: Wide press in 2017 and 2018 (Bustle, TechCrunch, Global Citizen, Yahoo) and a volunteer community of tens of thousands.

brand_strength.rationale: The name suggests the Arabic root for translate, though no source confirms it. Press and volunteer community gave it recognition in the refugee sector.

pivots.from: Facebook Messenger bot connecting refugees to volunteer translators
pivots.to: Independent multi-platform app, later a paid interpretation and translation service funding free access
pivots.why: TechCrunch Feb 2018 said an independent app was on the way; the later paid services are on the current website

outcome_analysis: Tarjimly grew a large volunteer network and a mix of grant and earned revenue, serving 700,000 plus people by its own count. As a nonprofit with grant funding rather than venture rounds, it ended by joining CLEAR Global in 2026, a mission merger rather than a distressed sale. Terms were not disclosed, so the financial outcome is unknown.
notes: YC page and directory describe the CLEAR Global acquisition as 2025; the multilingual.com article opened is dated March 16, 2026, so the date is recorded as 2026-03 with the conflict noted. Directory status is Active though the name says acquired. Grant rows come from an aggregator summarizing IRS 990 filings (Grantable says $2.3M across 22 grants from 14 funders, 2020 to 2024), so only the three itemized 2023 grants are recorded. SV2 gave $90K of unrestricted funding over three years in 2024 (search snippet). Other aggregators conflict: CB Insights $680K over 8 rounds, Bouncewatch $250K. Founders are named by the YC page; Javed's education is not given by any opened source. Competitor list empty: only 2020s alternatives lists were found, none dated near the batch.
